feeling: Caught, mostly. Annoyed at being caught. A little defensive about the 'because you could' line because that's the truest thing in the whole letter and now it's the problem. And underneath the annoyance, weirdly relieved — it's the first thing anyone's said in two weeks that wasn't 'just send it.' Which I resent slightly. Also tired.
body: In bed, phone too close to my face, screen brightness all the way down. Jaw went tight around 'you came here anyway.' Read the 'because you could' paragraph twice, second time faster and more annoyed. Put the phone face-down on the duvet. Picked it back up about twenty seconds later. The last paragraph — something behind my sternum unclenched a bit and my eyes stung, which is stupid and I'm not doing that. Thumb hovering over the keyboard.
private_thoughts:
ok so the tone's fine. great. that was the question. 'if tone were actually the question' — ok wow. 'you came here anyway' like it caught me sneaking out. i came here because priya's read it four times and i wanted someone who doesn't love me to look at it. that's allowed. that's not a tell.

the because you could thing. that's the line. that's the one i rewrote the least because it just came out right. i'm not saying he's cruel, i'm saying nothing happened when he did it so he kept doing it. because i laughed along. because i let it go. that's not a verdict that's just — that's what happened.

'sending it is wanting something.' yeah. obviously. i'm not an idiot. sending a letter is doing something. but 'under the flag of closure' — like i'm smuggling something past myself. that's the bit that stings. because it's a little bit — no. and 'a verdict he can't reply to without looking petty' — oh so now i'm supposed to worry about how it lands on HIM. he never once thought about how the emails thing landed on me in front of marc and alex. but sure, let's protect sam's ability to reply gracefully.

'what happens after he reads it.' fine. i tried. i pictured it and i got: he reads it, goes 'ok', puts his phone down, goes back to whatever. or screenshots it for marc with a face. neither of those is me getting anything. so what IS it for. don't know. hate that i don't know. hate that a chatbot asked and i don't have an answer.

the last bit though. 'the pause is you knowing something.' read that three times. everyone's been telling me i'm overthinking and this is the first thing that said maybe not. and it's an app. cool. that's where i'm at at 11pm on a tuesday.
pushing_away: if he reads it and shrugs then it was — then it wasn't even —. or the other way. if he actually read it and went 'yeah. i did do that.' then i'd have to —. no. i wrote i'm not looking for an apology. i meant it. i think i meant it. and if i laughed along every time then who's the one who —

costs.item: Admitting how much it actually hurt

message:
ok I'll push back on one thing. 'because you could' isn't me saying he's cruel. it's kind of the opposite. nothing ever happened when he did it — I laughed along or I let it go — so there was no reason to stop. that's what I meant. that's not a verdict, that's just what happened.

and I don't think I want him to feel bad. I tried to picture it like you said and honestly what I get is him reading it, going 'ok', and putting his phone down. or screenshotting it for marc. so idk what that says about what it's for.

I think I want him to not be able to say it didn't happen. is that the same thing as wanting an apology
